display.title: The Rambam and the Contest of Colors
display.summary_short: For the Rambam's yahrzeit, why no one can describe the days of Moshiach, and how the Rambam exposed jealous doctors who claimed to cure a man born blind.
display.summary_long: On the eve of Chof Teves, the Rambam's yahrzeit, the storyteller describes the Rambam's Mishneh Torah and Moreh Nevuchim, and notes that the Alter Rebbe, whose yahrzeit comes four days later, likewise gave us a Shulchan Aruch and the Tanya. He then explains the Rambam's description of the days of Moshiach: no war, hunger or pain, and a pleasure so great that one minute of Olam Haba outweighs seventy years of the best life in this world. Why can't our Sages describe it? Try explaining colors to a man born blind. The story: jealous palace doctors tell the king that the Rambam foolishly claims no medicine can cure a man born blind, and the king sets a thirty-day contest. The doctors bring a 'blind' man with sworn witnesses and 'cure' him, but the Rambam holds up a red cloth and a blue cloth, and the man names both colors. How could someone who never saw a color know its name? The tricksters are thrown out. Our eyes, too, are not yet ready for the light of the Geulah, and every mitzvah may be the one that brings it.
display.lesson: We cannot yet imagine the goodness of the days of Moshiach, and every mitzvah we do may be the one that brings the Geulah.
